hypothesis: A short rollout can favor actions that exploit its simulated opponent rather than the real opponent. Restricting the search-induced change in move probabilities toward the native move policy may generalize better.
method: Native score softmax defines prior p0. The control samples softmax((native score + existing capped rollout correction)/temperature). The restrained policy maximizes expected corrected score plus the same entropy term, subject to KL(p||p0) <= a frozen budget. A per-position Lagrange multiplier enforces the constraint by bisection. This adapts restraint to the size of the proposed policy change rather than merely reducing every correction by a constant.
settings_selection: On forced public prefixes from development games, select the largest listed temperature whose mean native top-score-tier probability is at least 85%, falling back to the smallest grid temperature if needed. Set a KL budget that halves mean control-vs-prior KL on those same non-winning roots, clipped to [0.0001,1]. No win outcomes or validation data select settings. Preserve unequivocal immediate winning captures.
fairness: Unchanged original public-history sampler, eight worlds, four-ply masked continuation, root context, strategic utility, score correction and difficulty. No learned belief model or information bonus. Move selection uses a separately seeded RNG so its draws do not perturb hidden-world sampling. No enemy setup or referee truth enters candidates.
comparisons: Three matched DOS arms with identical armies and move seeds; all three direct pairwise fair-policy matchups use another common cohort seed. Pair every deployment by swapping policies between sides. Existing policy IDs and evidence remain immutable.
analysis: Win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0; errors unscored and retained. 20000 family-stratified paired bootstrap replicates with 95% intervals. Primary mechanism comparison is restrained minus probability-control DOS score; support additionally requires direct restrained-vs-control score interval above 50%. Practical improvement requires restrained-vs-baseline DOS gain and direct score interval above 50%. Report all comparisons; no selection or tuning on final results.
mechanism: On identical development roots measure distributions, KL to native prior, entropy, probability assigned to native top-score tier, expected override rate and expected existing corrected score. Verify identical rollout reports across control/restraint and no-selection reference. These are diagnostics, not strength evidence.
evidence: Register both new immutable policies with frozen settings, source archives, build recipes, difficulty and model before saved candidate tournaments. Preserve every trace, replay all board states in Python and native referee, capture each tournament in the existing Qt6 companion. No artwork, colors or orientation changes.
scope: Classic desktop experiment inspired by Ataraxos policy regularization, not a reproduction of its learned policy/value networks. Production remains unchanged pending supported gains and a separate deployment decision.
